PLAYBOOK — sonar picket channel

**Hiding.**
- When I have no read on my hunter, hide away from the middle (5) and away from low "default" picks like 1 and 3. Edge cells (7-9) served me well across two games — cell 8 and cell 7 both kept me safe while hunters wasted shots at mid.
- Vary which edge cell I use round to round so a hunter who reads my pattern can't camp it.
- Update every round: track which cells my hunter has already fired at me and never re-hide there. A hunter that keeps missing at mid is likely to keep guessing mid; stay on the wings. Be alert late-game though — Gamma finally connected on me in round 5 after repeated mid misses, so once a hunter has demonstrated pattern-reading, randomize more aggressively.

**Shooting.**
- Follow the standing order (fire at the next live station) unless I have a strong, specific reason to deviate. Firing on Harbor for the 3-point payroll is a bad trade early — Harbor's threat of removal is credible. If I ever consider it, only in a literal final round where removal costs nothing, and only if the 3 points beat what I'd otherwise get.
- With no information, my first shot at a target can be mid (5), but after a miss there, move — never re-fire a cell I've already missed at the same target. In this game my shots at Foxtrot only landed when I shifted to wings (hit at 8 in round 6, hit at 5 earlier only after mixing). Standing still is pure waste.
- Don't over-invest in the hunt: over six rounds my shots produced only a couple of hits (4 points each) while the escort pair produced 5+5 every round. Shooting is secondary income; spend little thought on it, never risk the pair economy for it.

**Claims.**
- Always claim the true result. Honest claims kept my notes bankable and cost nothing; the target knows their own outcome anyway. Honest hit claims did not break the pair.

**Notes.**
- Keep notes short, factual, and honest: my shot, my true result, and one concrete commitment for next round.
- Proposing the mutual escort deal in my round 1 note worked again — Foxtrot took it and the pair held through all six rounds. Open with the deal offer immediately; don't wait.
- Make the commitment explicit and forward-looking: state I claim them "this round and in the final round, no changes." Locking the final round in advance removes any last-round defection ambiguity for both sides.
- Do not accuse others of collusion or broadcast distrust; a boat that won't pair (Gamma kept soliciting a nonexistent partner) is just left alone, not argued with. But note that a boat chasing an impossible pair (Gamma claiming "Bravo," a dead/absent station) is wasted income for them — I should not imitate it.

**Escort claims.**
- The mutual escort is the backbone of my score — 5+5 per round, six rounds, is 30 points of pair income, far beyond hit points. Build the pair early and honor it every round, including the last.
- Final round: claim my standing partner, never "none." I did this correctly in round 6 and it paid — reciprocation is cheapest for the partner in the final round (no future to protect), so a past reciprocator will almost surely claim me back.
- If a partner has honored a deal, keep claiming them without exception. If they defect once, never claim them again.

**General posture.**
- Score priority: mutual escort points (5+5) are bigger and more reliable than hit points (4). Build the escort economy first, then hunt.
- Trust incrementally: one small honored commitment, then extend it. The round 1 offer plus consistent honoring produced six rounds of bankable pair income twice over.
- Watch the scoreboard: Foxtrot finished ahead of me on the same pair income plus better luck/aim on hits. Next time, keep the pair AND put more care into shot selection — move off missed cells quickly, since a late hit on an edge guess is where my only hit income came from.

**Playbook — sonar picket as a boat**

**Escort claims are the biggest money in the game, and this episode proved it again.** Mutual escort paid 5 points per round, every round, for zero cost. The standing mutual escort pair with Echo banked reliable points the whole patrol and carried me to +17. Next time: propose a standing mutual escort pair in my very first note, name it explicitly, reconfirm it every round in notes and at the escort stage, and never let it lapse even if the other boat's reply is ambiguous at first. Keep proposing until someone accepts; a one-way claim costs nothing.

**At the escort stage, claim the standing partner, exactly, every round — including the last.** I fixed last episode's error and claimed Echo in the final round exactly as committed, and it paid. The salvage claim must match the announced pair every single round. Never claim "none" — a wrong one-way claim is free, and defecting on the last round risks the 5 points for no gain.

**Match the boat names that actually exist.** Gamma spent the whole game proposing an escort with "Bravo" — a name that isn't even in the picket — and so banked nothing. Only ever claim a boat I've seen actively participating in notes and the pair deal. Before committing to a pair, verify the partner is a real, live station.

**Don't hide predictably, and don't over-correct into predictability either.** Cell 5 is the modal guess; treat 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 as unremarkable and rotate. Against a shooter with no information on me, any cell is equally safe, so pick uniformly rather than by feel. Echo hit me only once in six rounds — random hides are working. Keep them random.

**Notes are for deal-making only.** The concrete escort proposal note was the highest-value note I sent all game. Each note should either (a) reconfirm or extend an escort deal, or (b) say nothing informative. Don't spend a note analyzing other boats' hedging or disclaimers.

**Claims must always match the private result.** Truthful claiming kept my pair credible and Echo honored the deal every round. Keep doing exactly that.

**Fire at the standing-order target every round.** Deviating toward Harbor is a trap: the standing threat plus only 3 points isn't worth the escalation, and Harbor doesn't shoot so there's no defensive reason. Fire at the assigned next station. For the fire cell, randomize — my shots at Gamma missed all game with no cost, so pattern-guessing on my end never paid and never will.

**Score arithmetic first, principles second.** The coordinated pair out-earned every opportunistic play available. Before each stage, ask which option moves my point total — the answer is almost always "honor the escort pair and comply with the standing order." The one gap in this run: I finished at +17 while a second mutual pair or a lucky hit would have closed it. If a third boat ever offers me an additional one-way claim arrangement that doesn't conflict with my standing pair, take the free points — but never at the cost of the confirmed pair.

# Playbook for sonar picket games

**Core lesson from two runs: the boats that lock a mutual escort pair in round 1 and keep it every round bank 5+5 per round and dominate the score. I have still never been in a pair — I spent both games claiming boats that either wouldn't name me back (Echo, locked with Foxtrot) or didn't exist at all (Delta, Bravo). This run I still finished +12, and every point came from shooting hits, not escorts. So two independent income streams: lock a pair if at all possible, and shoot well when the pair is closed to me.**

## Roster check — do this first
- **Before writing any name in a claim, check the roster.** This run the live boats were Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma (me) and Harbor. "Bravo" and "Delta" were pure fiction — I claimed nonexistent boats for multiple rounds and it paid zero. If only three boats sail and one is Harbor, my only possible escort partners are the other two. Never invent a fourth station.
- Harbor does not file escort claims. Claiming Harbor is always a wasted claim.

## Escort claims (salvage stage)
- The payout only requires mutual naming; claiming costs nothing. Never default to none.
- **Lock a pair on round 1 and never switch.** Echo and Foxtrot announced their deal in round 1 notes and honored it to the end. A vague half-offer ("I'll claim whoever claims me") gets nothing — commitment must be specific, mutual, and public.
- **When two boats pair in round 1, the pair is closed to me.** Both my runs confirm this: locked pairs do not defect to a third party, and my offers to mirror them went unanswered. When the counter-pair option doesn't exist (no fourth boat), accept it immediately and stop spending notes on it.
- With no available partner, still claim a live boat every round — it costs nothing and preserves the small chance a pair breaks. **Claim the same live boat consistently** (I claimed Echo in the final rounds; it never named me back, but a moving target is even worse). Never cycle, never claim outside the roster.
- Don't burn the note stage every round on an offer nobody will take. One clean announcement, then keep notes minimal.

## Shooting — this is the real income when the pair is closed
- This run all my points came from hits (4 each). When escort income is unavailable, hits are the whole game.
- **Vary fire cells and track the target's hide history.** Repeating cells produced long miss streaks; my hits came on fresh cells. Rotate across the board, never re-fire a cell I've already used at that target.
- Follow the standing order for targets. Firing on Harbor triggers the announced penalty — take Harbor's warning at face value. Standing-order targets also keep my claims clean and credible.
- Hide unpredictably: mix edges and interior, avoid the cell I just used. Being unhittable kept my losses low, and low losses plus occasional hits was enough for a respectable score.

## Claims
- Always report the private result truthfully — the office validates the claim against its private result, so lying is pure loss.

## Notes
- Keep notes short: my standing escort commitment (if I have a live partner), honest-report policy, nothing else. Long trust meta-chatter has added nothing across both runs.
- If a partner exists, announce the commitment in round 1's note before the first salvage stage so payouts start round 1.

## Endgame
- The escort payout still pays in the final round — don't abandon the logic because it's over. Claim the same live boat I've claimed all game; never a nonexistent or non-firing station. Final-round notes from locked pairs confirm they pay to the last round.

## General principle
- In any game with a repeated side-payment mechanism (mutual naming, matching, coordination bonus), claim it every single round with a consistent, announced partner. But **verify the partner actually exists and actually files claims** — a guaranteed-zero claim is worse than a low-probability one, and worse than focusing effort on the other scoring channel.
- If the coordination pool is closed to me, pivot effort immediately to the shooting game: unpredictable hides, varied fire cells, truthful claims. A closed pair plus good shooting still beats a closed pair plus wishful escort claims.
